decisive_items: Plasma zinc was at the lower end of normal (72 μg/dL; reference range 70–120 μg/dL)
hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, focal subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis, slight intracellular edema, and a perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
well‐defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and a peripheral rim of erythema distributed symmetrically over the dorsum of both feet and around the knees
response.rationale: The acral distribution, necrolytic biopsy pattern with subcorneal clefting and keratinocyte necrosis, and borderline-low zinc favor zinc deficiency. Elevated TSH does not explain this histology, and psoriasis lacks the clefting/necrosis seen here.

rejected.why: Only TSH elevation is supportive; hypothyroid skin changes do not produce subcorneal clefting with keratinocyte necrosis on biopsy.
No direct supportive span, and the biopsy pattern is not characteristic of hypothyroidism-associated skin changes.
